bucket: circle entries depict stronger individualized teacher engagement, small‑school/family‑like community ties, named supportive staff, and active parental volunteerism more than square entries
definition: Circle reviewers repeatedly report small classes, teachers who go the extra mile, mentorship from coaches and named exemplary teachers, multi‑generation enrollment, and active parent volunteers ('teachers go that extra mile', 'everyone is treated as family', 'I volunteered in the front office'), signaling personalized support and tight community bonds not emphasized in Square reviews.

bucket: circle entries report more operational, facility, scheduling, funding and process failures (lost records, overcrowding, transportation, food, tech, gradebook and parent‑communication breakdowns) than square entries
definition: This bucket holds concrete logistics and resource problems—underfunding/overcrowding, lost student records, broken gradebooks/parent portals, inadequate supplies or transportation, problematic cafeteria food and scheduling/locker logistics. Examples: “overcrowded and underfunded,” “they had lost over half of her school records…couldn’t walk,” “No supplies! No books! Computers don't work!,” and “refused to give access to parent portal / try calling the school you WILL NEVER get anyone to answer.”

bucket: circle entries allege more administrative mismanagement, favoritism/nepotism, corruption, inconsistent enforcement, and lack of accountability than square entries
definition: This groups governance and operational complaints about leadership and policy (e.g., 'superintendent...is related to EVERYBODY,' 'corruption…shocks me,' 'monitoring of the teachers. There is NONE,' 'the NAME GAME around here,' 'no response whatsoever from principal and superintendent') that circle reviewers raise much more than square reviewers.

bucket: circle entries report stronger, concrete academic rigor, advanced-course pathways, STEM/technical offerings, and documented college‑prep outcomes (AP/IB, scholarships, counselors) than square entries
definition: Many circle reviews enumerate measurable academic assets—high AP/IB participation and success rates, robust college counseling (full‑time counselors, college visits), scholarship totals, engineering/STEM programs and early college credit—that are tied to clear outcomes (college matriculation, AP credits), whereas square reviews generally give vaguer claims about academics or note weak STEM labs and remediation needs.

bucket: circle entries report more frequent and severe student-safety and misconduct incidents (bullying, fights, drugs, assaults) with visible adult non‑intervention than square entries
definition: This bucket captures descriptions of pervasive peer-on-peer harm and immediate safety threats (daily fights, robberies, on-campus drug dealing, sexual activity on campus, bus assaults, near-weekly lockdowns) together with accounts that adults/security often fail to stop or appropriately remediate the incidents (e.g., videos of a 13‑year‑old beaten while a bus driver watched; reports that ‘bullying happens every second of the day’ and bathrooms smell of vapor). These raw terms contrast with square entries that either omit such incidents or describe low levels of fights/drugs and cooperative security.

bucket: square entries describe a far wider and deeper set of specialized academic pathways and extracurricular offerings (IB/AP/magnets/dual‑enrollment, vocational tracks, award‑winning arts and nationally ranked teams) than circle entries
definition: This bucket captures programmatic breadth: many square reviews list named pathways and offerings (International Baccalaureate, STEM/Math‑Science academies, AP/dual‑enrollment, ROTC, marching band, choir, robotics, CTE certificates and internships), whereas circle reviews rarely enumerate comparable advanced tracks or specialty extracurriculars and instead give only general program comments.

bucket: square entries describe a broader and more numerous set of academic and extracurricular programs and structured pathways (AP/IB/honors, vocational CTE, arts, ROTC, magnet/choice, dual‑enrollment) than circle entries
definition: Many square reviews enumerate concrete programmatic offerings — AP/IB/honors tracks, Choice/STEM/Performing Arts academies, ROTC/JROTC, FFA, vocational shops, dual‑enrollment/early‑college, award‑winning music and DECA/FBLA teams — whereas circle reviews rarely list such a wide catalogue of curricular or extracurricular pathways.

bucket: square entries report more frequent and severe student safety, behavior, and substance incidents (bullying, fights, drugs, sexual misconduct, gangs, lockdowns) than circle entries
definition: This bucket captures reviews that describe concrete safety crises and ongoing student misconduct—e.g., repeated fights and weekly lockdowns, “high drug problems,” sexualized behavior on campus, gang activity, weapons, and multiple accounts where staff did nothing when bullying/drug incidents were reported. Falling into this bucket means the school narrative centers on acute threats to student physical/psychological safety and regular on‑campus incidents rather than isolated misbehavior.

bucket: square entries report more chronic resource, staffing, and facility constraints (overcrowding, teacher shortages/uncertified staff, outdated materials, pests, food/service shortfalls) that impair instruction than circle entries
definition: Numerous square reviews describe missing textbooks/desks, classes without teachers, uncertified or inexperienced instructors, overcrowded classrooms, budget cuts, pest/cleanliness problems, and counseling understaffing; circle reviews seldom present such persistent operational/resource deficits. Representative claims include: “no money for books or desks,” “class sizes of over 40,” “3 classes that have no teachers,” and “cockroaches in the cafeteria.”

bucket: square entries report more concrete facility, capacity, and operational problems (overcrowding, construction/lunch/transport logistics, HVAC, outdated resources) than circle entries
definition: This bucket groups tangible infrastructure and daily‑operations complaints: severe overcrowding and crowded hallways, construction disruption to instruction, awkward scheduling (eighth‑period lunch, block scheduling conflicts), transportation/pickup burdens, HVAC and building disrepair, and missing curricular offerings (drivers ed), as in “way overcrowded,” “construction makes it almost impossible to learn,” “eighth period lunch…entire day without food,” and “textbooks looked outdated.”
